core.title: Bind produce/consume contracts to registered contract identities
core.given: Plan artifacts declare produce/consume entries for each module; an authored contract registry is the single source of truth for each contract's identity, path, theme, producers and consumers.
core.when: You author, change, review or validate produce/consume entries, their contract references, or registry entries.
core.then: Every non-null contract reference on a produce or consume entry must, after stripping its URN prefix, resolve to an identity registered in the contract registry.
prefer: Add new contract identities to the registry through its authoring flow, so the registry entry carries identity, path, theme, producers and consumers.
Mandatory (null-cross-edge invariant): give the producing entry of every cross-module edge (an artifact name produced by one module and consumed by a different module) a non-null registered contract.
Mandatory (unconsumed invariant): mark a produced non-null contract that no other module consumes with the external-consumption marker.
avoid: Contract URNs whose identity, after stripping the URN prefix, is absent from the registry (typos, renamed or deleted contracts). A prefixed URN is valid exactly when its stripped identity is a registry key.
A null contract on a cross-module producer (dangling producer — no contract binds the edge); a required invariant, not optional.
A produced non-null contract that no other module consumes and that is not marked external; a required invariant, not optional.
Silencing findings by nulling a contract reference or by marking an internally consumed contract external.
unless: A produced contract with no consuming module is coherent if marked external (this exempts only the unconsumed invariant).
core.why: The registry owns contract identity and producer/consumer ownership; unregistered URNs, null-bound cross-module edges and orphan producers let the plan graph and the registry drift.
evidence: The registry-coherence check passes with no findings of any of the three kinds (all three invariants are required).
A reviewer can map every contract URN in the plan artifacts, after stripping its prefix, to a key in the contract registry.
Every cross-module edge has a non-null contract on its producing entry; every produced non-null contract has another consuming module or the external marker.
verification: Registry keys are contract identities; the contract URN prefix is stripped before lookup.
Unregistered identity: every non-null contract URN on any produce or consume entry must strip to an existing registry identity.

Null cross-module edge: edges are keyed on artifact name — a name produced by one module and consumed by a different module; the producing entry must declare a non-null contract (a null contract there is a dangling producer). Same-module produce/consume is not a cross-module edge.
Unconsumed: every produce entry with a non-null contract must be consumed by at least one other module or carry the external-consumption marker.

All three invariants are checked across the whole plan graph — every plan artifact's produce/consume entries against the contract registry. Exemptions are per-invariant: a null contract on a non-cross edge exempts only the null-cross-edge invariant; the external marker exempts only the unconsumed invariant.

values: contract field changed (including set to null)
null contract on a cross-module edge (dangling producer)
produced contract with no consumer and not marked external

fires: A planner adds a consume entry whose contract URN strips to an identity not present in the contract registry.
A planner adds a produce entry for an artifact name that another module consumes, with a null contract reference.
A produce entry declares a non-null contract that no other module consumes and that is not marked external.
A contract is renamed or removed from the registry while plan artifacts still reference its identity.

A planner reviews or validates existing plan artifacts that already contain an unregistered identity, a null-contract cross-module producer, or an unconsumed non-external produced contract — even without editing them.
doesNotFire: Null-cross-edge only: a produce entry with a null contract whose artifact name is not consumed by any other module is exempt from the null-cross-edge invariant; the rule is inactive only if the registered-identity and unconsumed invariants also hold for the rest of the graph.

Unconsumed only: a produced contract consumed by no module but explicitly marked external is exempt from the unconsumed invariant; its URN must still resolve to a registered identity, and the null-cross-edge invariant must still hold elsewhere.
Edits to plan artifact fields unrelated to produce/consume (e.g. descriptions) that leave contract references unchanged — only when the graph already satisfies all three invariants.
Changes outside the plan artifacts and the contract registry, when the existing graph already satisfies all three invariants.

proposedKeys.meaning: Path of the single authored contract registry that is the source of truth for contract identities and their producer/consumer ownership.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No key locates the contract registry: it is not a plan item (layout.plan_item), not a source/test/e2e root, and not the repository config (roots.config).

proposedKeys.meaning: The syntax by which a plan artifact's produce/consume entry references a contract: a contract field that holds a contract URN (its prefix is stripped to obtain the registered identity) or null.
proposedKeys.bunValue: contract: URN / contract: null; strip the 'contract:' URN prefix before lookup
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The urn.binding.<artifact> family describes a source or test file binding ITSELF to an artifact (header comment, decorator, annotation) — it does not cover a plan-artifact entry referencing an external contract identity, with null allowed and a URN prefix stripped to normalize the identity. No other urn or idiom key covers a plan entry's contract-reference syntax and identity normalization, so a new idiom key (not an extension of the self-binding family) is proposed.

proposedKeys.meaning: The marker on a produced contract that declares it consumed outside the plan graph (exempts the unconsumed invariant only).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group covers request, gate, import and machinery constructs only; nothing describes the external-consumption marker of a produced contract.

proposedKeys.meaning: The authoring flow or command that adds a contract identity to the registry.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: tooling.urn_resolver resolves URNs but no key names the flow that authors registry entries.

neutralityNotes: 'Wagon' is the ATDD-Bun name for a bounded product slice; the core says 'module' and the mapping back is carried by the profile's wagon concept (layout.wagon_dir). Finding and validator ids (UNREGISTERED, NULL-CROSS-WAGON, UNCONSUMED, test_contract_registry_coherence) are realization details kept bunOnly; the core names the three invariants generically (registered identity, null cross-module edge, unconsumed) while preserving that all three are mandatory and that exemptions apply per invariant. The rule cannot be instantiated without four proposed profile keys (registry path, plan-entry contract-reference syntax, external marker, registry authoring flow); until approved, bun.json remains the worked example. Bun-side metadata with no core counterpart (audit, trace, additions, splitSuggestion) stays in the realization; the split suggestions would equally split the neutral core's prefer/avoid/unless/verification entries.
